items.item_text: Required to hold a valid California driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program
Bachelor's Degree or Equivalent: Social Sciences, Scientific, Computational Science, or Related Field
There is no minimum of years of experience related to healthcare, laboratory, and/or clinical research required for this position.

1-3 years of experience in (1) working with older adults in clincial or research settings, (2) conducting research in health science, (3) emotion, social behaviors, health, and psychophysiology (saliva sample collection and management), (4) in-home interview research, and (5) computer programming and/or data management.

This position in the Social relationships, Health, and Altruism Research (SHARE) Lab will provide opportunities to be involved in all aspects of the research project(s) to examine empathy and dyadic processes between clinical populations and their family members (e.g., spousal caregivers) with an emphasis in multi-method data collection, behavioral coding, and participant recruitment, research visit facilitation, and data collection as well as analysis, and, if applicable, preparing for graduate training in either basic science, clinical/health science, or both.
20% - Data Collection, Management, and Quality Review
5% - Research Coordination and Other Assigned Duties
1. ability to work with a interdisciplinary team of researchers. 2. professionalism and courtesy in all interactions with lab members, department staff, and supervisors.

1. Familiarity with the laboratory's computer programs (e.g., SPSS, REDCap, Qualtrics, Microsoft Office) for data entry, data sharing, questionnaire creation, and study packet design. 2. Familiarity with writing computer codes for designing tasks, data management, and/or data analyses. 3. Ability to install, operate, and troubleshoot lab equipment. Organize training and inter-departmental meetings to facilitate approval and installation of equipment/devices for data collection. 4. Familiarity with preparing and submitting documents, such as Institutional Review Board protocols. 5. Familiarity with saliva sample collection and management.
